**Two cold reviews found 5 blockers in #682's slices — three of my own claims were false**

**What**: Adversarial cold reviews of PR #740 (slice 1) and PR #741 (slice 2) returned 5 blockers and 10 corrections between them. Every claim I re-verified independently held. Neither slice should merge as-is.

**Where**: `brain/scripts/review/cli.mjs`, `evaluators/inferential.mjs`, `evaluators/refuter.mjs`, `lib/resolve-challenger.mjs`, `vcs/governance-tiers.mjs`, `test/review-regulated/regulated-review.e2e.test.mjs`, `openspec/changes/issue-682-independence-axis-ruling/`.

**THREE CLAIMS I MADE THAT ARE FALSE — the entries worth keeping:**
1. **"REQ-682-2 protects #435's credential-free install."** `resolveTier({})` returns `standard`, not `lite` (REQ-TIER-10), and `config-migrations.mjs:116` forbids defaulting to lite. A fresh install lands on `standard` where I set the producer ON with `same-model`. `test/fresh-install/in-container.sh` never invokes `brain:review` either. Correct behaviour, invented cause — the `#675 M1` class the ticket itself cites.
2. **"Slice 2 delivers REQ-682-3."** It does not. `resolveAxis`'s value is discarded at `cli.mjs:497` (`!== null`, used as a boolean), nothing puts the axis on the wire, and NO task in ANY slice delivers it. The requirement was dropped in decomposition and the PR body asserted it delivered. What slice 2 actually delivers is #683's controls union — a different requirement.
3. **"What the challenger receives is a subset of what the verdict renders."** False as shipped: `title` is in `CARRIED_FIELDS` and `renderVerdict` emits it nowhere (`rg` over verdict.mjs/parse-verdict.mjs/schema-v2.mjs returns zero hits); `file`/`line` render only when `hasUsableAnchor` passes. And the test asserted `CARRIED_FIELDS.includes(k)` — **comparing the list to itself**, which cannot fail for any member however un-rendered. A tautological assertion.

**THE WORST DEFECT — my own tier values recreate #552's ruled-against state.** The producer's gate is `inferentialEnabled`; the challenger's gate is `protocol === 'brain-review/2'`. Measured: `standard` is `{inferentialEnabled: true, reviewProtocol: 'brain-review/1'}` — **they disagree at a shipped tier default**. At `standard` the producer runs, `applyCausalAdmission` is skipped entirely, and the verdict declares `controls_not_applied: []` (the judgment control WAS applied) with no refuter outcome, no condition, no escalation. That is exactly the state #682 exists to prevent.

**Other confirmed defects:** a producer-chosen `id` colliding with a deterministic gate finding downgrades the REAL gate blocker to `correction` when the reasoned claim is refuted (fail-open); a reasoned blocker does not block because `evaluateInferential`'s `conclusion` is discarded in the merge; `Array.isArray(generated) ? generated : []` folds "model unreachable" into "found nothing", pre-breaking acceptance criterion 6 in the file whose header rails against it; a runner answering for only some blockers leaves the rest unmarked; `unbuiltRunner`'s call-time throw is caught nowhere and replaces #552's posted fail-closed REVISE with an unhandled rejection.

**THE METHOD LESSON, and it is the durable one.** Both reviewers named the same root cause independently: **my mutations varied the units and never the composition.** Slice 1's six all varied behaviour inside `resolveChallenger`; none varied whether `cli.mjs` calls it — replacing the call with `null` leaves the full suite green at 4094/4094. Slice 2's five all varied `inferential.mjs` in isolation; all four blockers live in the wiring. Unvaried axes they named: the protocol, the axis (the one composition test hard-codes `human`, the only implemented one), the renderer, the id space, the conclusion, field VALUES rather than names (`line: 0`, a nested object under an allowed key), and the generator's failure modes.

**A ruling is not exempt from review because it was signed and merged.** #737 shipped with a false justification and the cold review caught it two PRs later.
